Article 2 (Definitions)
The term "electrical appliances" means industrially manufactured products that can be used by connecting to an alternating or direct current power source and components or parts of such products;

The term "consumer products" means industrially manufactured products for consumer use without additional processing (excluding simple assembling) and components or parts of such products (excluding electrical appliances);
The term "production" means manufacturing, assembling, or processing electrical appliances or consumer products for the purpose of distributing or renting them;

The term "safety control of products" means activities of controlling the production, importation, distribution, etc. of products to prevent hazards to the lives or health of consumers or damage to property or to the natural environment, which might arise in the course of handling and using products;
The term "safety certification" means certifying the safety of a product after testing the product and assessing the factory of the product;
The term "safety verification" means verifying whether a product conforms to safety standards as a result of a safety verification test conducted by a testing lab for safety verification;

The term "supplier's declaration of conformity" means a supplier's declaration that any of its products conforms to safety standards by voluntarily testing the product or by requesting a third party to test the product;
The term "product testing" means testing a product to verify the safety of the product itself;
The term "factory assessment" means assessing manufacturing facilities, testing facilities, technical capacity and manufacturing systems necessary for manufacturing products;

The term "safety inspection" means verifying whether safety standards are satisfied through an inspection conducted by an institution designated by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy pursuant to Article 34-2 (1) (hereinafter referred to as "safety inspection institution");
The term "products subject to safety certification" means the following electrical appliances and consumer products:

Electrical appliances subject to safety certification: Electrical appliances specified by and approved under Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through safety certification, where it is highly anticipated that the structure, usage, etc. of such electrical appliances will cause hazards, such as fire and electrocution;

Consumer products subject to safety certification: Consumer products specified by and approved under Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through safety certification, where it is highly anticipated that the structure, materials, usage, etc. of such consumer products will harm the lives and bodies of consumers or cause damage to property or to the natural environment;
The term "products subject to safety verification" means the following electrical appliances and consumer products:

Electrical appliances subject to safety verification: Electrical appliances specified and approved by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through product testing by an institution designated by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, where the structure, usage, etc. of such electrical appliances are likely to cause hazards, such as fire and electrocution;

Consumer products subject to safety verification: Consumer products specified and approved by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through product testing by an institution designated by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, where the structure, materials, usage, etc. of such consumer products are likely to harm the lives and bodies of consumers or cause damage to property or to the natural environment;
The term "products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity" means the following electrical appliances and consumer products:

Electrical appliances subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity: Electrical appliances specified and approved by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through product testing directly by a manufacturer or an importer or by a third party at the request of a manufacturer or an importer, where the structure, usage, etc. of such electrical appliances are likely to cause hazards, such as fire and electrocution;

Consumer products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity: Consumer products specified and approved by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through product testing directly by a manufacturer or an importer or by a third party at the request of a manufacturer or an importer, where such consumer products are likely to cause an accident or harm consumers, while consumers handle, use, carry or manage them otherwise or where it is difficult for consumers to identify the difference in ingredients, performance, specifications, etc.;

The term "consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards" means consumer products specified and approved by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those from which hazards can be prevented through the compliance with safety standards by the manufacturer or importer, where it is difficult for consumers to identify the difference in ingredients, performance, specifications, etc., although such consumer products are less likely to cause an accident or harm consumers, while consumers handle, use, carry or manage them otherwise;

The term "child protective packaging" means packages and containers designed and devised to make it difficult for children aged under five years to take out contents therein within a certain period of time, although it is not difficult for adults to open them;

The term "consumer products subject to child protective packaging" means consumer products specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those subject to child protective packaging, from among consumer products that are likely to cause hazards, such as poisoning, if a consumer drinks or inhales them;

The term "electrical appliances subject to safety inspection" means re-used electrical appliances (referring to those manufactured for the purpose of reusing used electrical appliances) where their structure, usage, etc. are likely to cause hazards, such as fire and electrocution, and which are prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as they are deemed to prevent such hazards through a safety inspection conducted by a safety inspection institution;

The term "buying services" means services provided by a person acting as an agent for a domestic consumer, upon the consumer's request for personal use, in the process of placing an order for a product sold overseas and paying the price for the product so as to make an arrangement with an overseas seller to dispatch the product directly to the consumer;

The term "parallel importation" means that a third party who is not the exclusive licensee for the market within the territory of the Republic of Korea imports products produced and distributed by the holder of an overseas trade mark (limited to commodities with a trade mark affixed and distributed by the person who has the legal right to use the trade mark in foreign countries) for the purpose of sales.
Article 3 (Product Safety Deliberation Committee)

In order to deliberate on the following matters for safety control of electrical appliances and consumer products, the Product Safety Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be established under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

The designation of products subject to safety certification, products subject to safety verification, products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity, consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards, consumer products subject to child protective packaging, and electrical appliances subject to safety inspection (hereinafter referred to as "products subject to safety control") and any change to such designation;
The establishment, amendment, etc. of safety standards for testing products subject to safety control;

Matters on which the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy requests the Committee to deliberate in connection with any action, measure, etc. taken against products subject to safety control but produced and distributed in violation of this Act;
Examination of the safety of electrical appliances and consumer products;
Comprehensive measures to be taken in response to accidents caused by electrical appliances and consumer products;
Matters on which the other statutes require deliberation by the Committee;
Other matters that the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy refers to the Committee for deliberation as important matters involving the policy for safety control of products.

The Committee shall be composed of not more than 25 members, including one chairperson; and the chairperson shall be elected by and from among committee members, while committee members shall consist of the following persons:

Persons appointed by the head of each administrative agency to which they belong, from among Grade III public officials and public officials equivalent to Grade III officials, who are in charge of affairs related to safety control of products in the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the Fair Trade Commission, or public officials who are members of the Senior Executive Service;

Persons appointed by the President of the Korea Consumer Agency, established pursuant to Article 33 of the Framework Act on Consumers , from among employees who are in charge of affairs related to safety control of products in the Korea Consumer Agency;

Persons commissioned by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, considering gender, from among persons recommended by organizations related to safety control of products, among non-profit, non-governmental organizations under Article 2 of the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act ;
Other persons commissioned by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, considering gender, from among persons who have abundant knowledge and experience in safety control of products.
The term of office of each committee member appointed or commissioned under paragraph (2) 3 or 4 shall be three years and may be renewed consecutively only once.

The Committee may have special committees for each segment of products subject to safety control in order to examine special matters concerning the establishment, amendment, etc. of safety standards for product testing.

Except as otherwise expressly provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4), matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Committee and special committees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
Article 4 (Designation of Safety Certification Body)

The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may designate a corporation or an organization as a body responsible for safety certification (hereinafter referred to as "safety certification body"), from among corporations or organizations that engage in a business related to safety control of products, in order to ensure the safety of products subject to safety certification.

A corporation or an organization that intends to be designated as a safety certification body shall meet the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree for designation, such as standards for testing facilities and human resources necessary for safety certification, and shall file an application for the designation with the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

A safety certification body may enter into agreements with domestic and foreign institutions testing the safety of products subject to safety certification, under which the results of product testing or factory assessment shall be recognized mutually, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Every safety certification body shall prepare and retain records of safety certification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may guide, supervise, and assist safety certification bodies to the extent necessary for ensuring the safety of products.
Article 5 (Safety Certification)

A manufacturer (including persons who export products produced in a foreign country to the Republic of Korea; hereinafter the same shall apply) or an importer of products subject to safety certification shall obtain safety certification for each model of such products (referring to the type of a product with its own name prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy; hereinafter the same shall apply) from a safety certification body, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

If a manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety certification intends to have a safety certification amended, the manufacturer or importer shall obtain an amended certification from a safety certification body, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the foregoing shall not apply where a manufacturer or importer makes a modification with respect to any of the matters specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy that are unrelated to the safety of the relevant product.

A safety certification body shall certify the safety of a product subject to safety certification, if the product meets the safety standards for product testing and the standards for factory assessment prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That a safety certification body may certify the safety of a product subject to safety certification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, if safety standards have not been publicly notified with respect to the product or the safety standards publicly notified are not applicable to the product.

When a safety certification body certifies the safety of a product under paragraph (3), it may attach conditions to the certification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy. The conditions attached in such cases shall not impose an unreasonable obligation upon the relevant manufacturer.
Article 6 (Exemption from Safety Certification)

Where any of the products specified by Presidential Decree is confirmed by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, from among products subject to safety certification, as a product manufactured or imported for the purpose of testing the product for research and development, exhibition, or safety certification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;

Where any of the products specified by Presidential Decree is confirmed by the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as "Mayor/ Do Governor"), from among products subject to safety certification, as a product imported for the purpose of exportation, as prescribed by Ordinance of the relevant Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as "City/ Do ");
Where a product subject to safety certification is manufactured for the purpose of exportation;

Where the safety of a product is certified by any of foreign safety certification bodies specified and publicly notified by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy under reciprocal recognition agreements between nations;

Where a safety certification body confirms conformity according to the results of a product test or factory assessment performed by a domestic or foreign institution with whom the safety certification body has entered into a recognition agreement under Article 4 (3);

Where a manufacturer or an importer that has a testing capacity equal to or higher than the level specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy tests a product, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, and the safety certification body confirms the conformity of the product;
Where the safety of a product subject to safety certification has been confirmed and is imported through parallel importation, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;
Where a product subject to safety certification is imported or manufactured only once, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;
Other cases specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those where safety has been approved under any other statute.
Article 7 (Periodic Inspections and Internal Inspections)

A safety certification body shall conduct a periodic inspection on the following matters once every two years, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in order to ascertain that the products subject to safety certification continue to remain safe after the safety of them was certified under Article 5 (1):
Products subject to safety certification;
Manufacturing facilities;
Testing facilities;
Technical capacity.

A manufacturer of products subject to safety certification shall conduct internal inspections on the products manufactured after the safety of such products was certified, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, and shall prepare and retain records of such inspections.
Article 8 (Safety Inspection of Imported Used Electrical Appliances subject to Safety Inspection)

A person who intends to import used electronic appliances subject to safety certification shall undergo a safety inspection to examine the safety of such electronic appliances subject to safety certification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the foregoing shall not apply where a person has obtained the safety certification under Article 5 (1) or where any of the grounds for the exemption from safety certification under Article 6 exists.
The safety standards under Article 5 (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the standards for the safety inspections under paragraph (1).
Article 9 (Safety Certification Mark)

A manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety certification shall put any of the following marks (hereinafter referred to as "safety certification mark or a similar mark") on the products subject to safety certification or the packages of such products, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy:
Products subject to safety certification with safety certified under Article 5 (1): The safety certification mark and the mark specified in the safety standards under Article 5 (3);
Products subject to safety certification but exempted from safety certification under Article 6 : The mark of exemption from safety certification;

Electrical appliances subject to safety certification with safety tested under Article 8 (1): The safety inspection mark and the mark specified in the standards for safety inspections under Article 8 (2).

No person shall put the safety certification mark or a similar mark on a product subject to safety certification and its package, unless the person has obtained safety certification under Article 5 (1), is exempted from safety certification under Article 6 , or has successfully passed a safety inspection under Article 8 (1).
Any of the following persons shall not modify or remove the safety certification mark or a similar mark from a product subject to safety certification, without permission:
The manufacturer, importer or import agent of a product subject to safety certification;
The distributor, sales broker or buying agent of a product subject to safety certification;
The rental business operator of a product subject to safety certification;
The person who produces a product by using a product subject to safety certification as a component or part;
Any of the following persons who use a product subject to safety certification:
An electric utility business operator as defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A person who installs electric installations for private use as defined in subparagraph 19 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A constructor as defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Electrical Construction Business Act ;
A person who uses a consumer product subject to safety certification for commercial purposes.

Where a person referred to in any subparagraph of paragraph (3) engages in the distribution, rental, sales brokerage (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce removes a product without the safety certification mark or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety certification mark or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information) or import agency through the Internet, the person shall publish information about safety certification in the relevant website so that consumers can find such information, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 10 (Prohibition of Distribution and, Use of Products subject to Safety Certification without Safety Certification Mark or Similar Mark)

A manufacturer, importer, distributor or rental service provider of products subject to safety certification shall neither sell or rent any product subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark, nor import, display or store such product for the purpose of selling or renting the product.

No sales broker, buying agent or import agent of products subject to safety certification shall act as a sales broker (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce removes a product without the safety certification mark or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety certification mark or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information), buying agent or import agent for the products subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark.
Any of the persons referred to in Article 9 (3) 4 through 6 shall not use a product subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark.
Article 11 (Revocation of Safety Certification)

In any of the following cases, a safety certification body may revoke the certification of a product of a manufacturer or an importer or may issue the manufacturer or an importer an order to forbid a manufacturer or an importer from using the safety certification mark or a similar mark for a period of not more than six months or an order to take measures for improvement: Provided , That safety certification shall be revoked in cases falling under subparagraph 1; and safety certification may be revoked or an order may be issued to prohibit the use of the safety certification mark or a similar mark in cases falling under subparagraph 10: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If a person is found to have obtained a safety certification by fraud or other improper means;
If a product subject to safety certification, which shall be manufactured after obtaining safety certification, fails to meet the safety standards under Article 5 (3);
If a person fails to put the safety certification mark or a similar mark or puts a false mark;
If a person fails to fulfill the conditions under Article 5 (4);
If a person rejects, interferes with, or evades a periodic inspection conducted under Article 7 (1);
If manufacturing facilities, testing facilities or technical capacity referred to in Article 7 (1) fails to meet the standards for factory assessment;
If a person fails to conduct internal inspections under Article 7 (2);
If a person fails to prepare and retain records of internal inspections under Article 7 (2) or enters and preserves false records of such inspections;
If a person violates an order issued under Article 40 (1) or (9);

If a person fails to comply with an order issued to forbid the person from using the safety certification mark or a similar mark or to require the person to make improvements in cases falling under subparagraphs 2 through 9.

When a safety certification body revokes a safety certification or issues an order to prohibit the use of the safety certification mark or a similar mark or an order for improvement, it shall publicly announce such fact, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

If a safety certification body revokes safety certification under paragraph (1), it shall not certify the safety of any identical model subject to safety certification during one year from the date of revocation.
Article 12 (Revocation, etc. of Designation of Safety Certification Body)

If a safety certification body falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may fully or partially revoke the designation of the body or may issue an order to fully or partially suspend its business operations for a specified period of not more than one year: Provided , That such designation shall be revoked in cases falling under subparagraph 1 or 2:
If it has been designated as a safety certification body by fraud or other improper means;
If a safety certification body continues safety certifications or safety inspections during the period of suspension of business operations after it is ordered to suspend business operations;
If a safety certification body fails to conduct safety certifications or safety inspections with no justification;
If a safety certification body violates any of methods, procedures, etc. of safety certifications or safety inspections in performing safety certifications or safety inspections;
If a safety certification body ceases to meet the standards for designation under Article 4 (2);
If a safety certification body fails to prepare and retain records of safety certifications or enters and keeps false records, in violation of Article 4 (4);
If a safety certification body violates safety standards or standards for factory assessment under Article 5 (3) in performing safety certifications;
If a safety certification body fails to take the measure prescribed in Article 11 (1), with no justification;
If a safety certification body issues a safety certification, in violation of Article 11 (3);
If a safety certification body charges a fee at a rate higher or lower than the rate specified under Article 43 .
The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall not designate a person as a safety certification body again within one year from the date the person has its designation revoked under paragraph (1).
Detailed criteria for the administrative dispositions under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 13 (Penalty Surcharges Imposed in Lieu of Suspension of Business Operations for Safety Certification)

Where the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall order a person to suspend business operations under any subparagraph of Article 12 (1) but finds that the suspension of business operations will cause severe inconvenience to users of the business, he or she may impose a penalty surcharge of not more than 300 million won upon the person, in lieu of the suspension of business operations.

Matters necessary for the amount of a penalty surcharge to be imposed under paragraph (1) for each type of violation according to the degree of violation, etc., the method of collecting such penalty surcharge, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

If a person who is obligated to pay a penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) fails to pay the penalty surcharge by payment deadline, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall collect the penalty surcharge in the same manner as delinquent national taxes are collected.
Article 14 (Designation of Testing Labs for Safety Verification)

In order to ensure the safety of products subject to safety verification, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may designate any of corporations and organizations that engage in a business related to product safety management as a lab (hereinafter referred to as "testing lab for safety verification") testing products for safety verification (hereinafter referred to as "tests for safety verification").

Any corporation or organization that intends to be designated as a testing lab for safety verification shall meet the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree for designation, including testing facilities and personnel for performing tests for safety verification, and shall apply for designation to the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

Any testing lab for safety verification may enter into an agreement with domestic and overseas institutions engaging in tests for the safety of products subject to safety verification for mutual recognition of the results of product tests, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Every testing lab for safety verification shall prepare and retain records of tests for safety verification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
In order to ensure the safety of products, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may guide, supervise, and assist testing labs for safety verification to the necessary extent.
Article 15 (Reporting of Products subject to Safety Verification)

A manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety verification shall have each model of the products subject to safety verification tested by a testing lab for safety verification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, have the relevant products confirmed by the lab as those that meet the safety standards under paragraph (4), and then report the confirmation to the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

When a manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety verification intends to make a change in regard to any of the facts described in the report submitted on safety verification under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "safety verification report"), he or she shall file a report on change with the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the foregoing shall not apply where a change is made with respect to any of the facts specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those irrelevant to the safety of products.

Upon receipt of a report or a report on change under paragraph (1) or the main clause of paragraph (2), the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall review the details thereof and accept such report if it conforms to this Act. <Added on Oct. 18, 2022>

Every testing lab for safety verification shall apply the standards determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy for the safety of products subject to safety verification when it conducts tests for safety verification: Provided , That a testing lab for safety verification may conduct tests for safety verification on products subject to safety verification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, if there are no safety standards publicly notified for a specific product subject to safety verification or if it is impracticable to apply the safety standards publicly notified to a specific product subject to safety verification. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

When a manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety verification files a report or a report on change pursuant to paragraph (1) or the main clause of paragraph (2), he or she shall keep documents demonstrating that the relevant products subject to safety verification conform to the safety standards under paragraph (4), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
Article 16 (Exemption from Duty to Report Safety Verification)

Where a person has obtained confirmation from the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy on the products specified by Presidential Decree, among those subject to safety verification, and produced or imported for the purpose of research and development, exhibition, or testing of products for reporting safety verification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;

Where a person has obtained confirmation from a Mayor/ Do Governor on the products specified by Presidential Decree, among those subject to safety verification, and produced or imported for the purpose of exportation, as prescribed by municipal ordinance of the relevant City/ Do ;
Where products subject to safety verification are produced for the purpose of exportation;

Where the relevant products have been confirmed by a domestic or overseas institution, with whom a testing lab for safety verification has an agreement for mutual recognition under Article 14 (3), as conforming products as a result of a product test conducted by the institution;

Where a testing lab for safety verification verifies the relevant products as conforming products according to the results of a test conducted by the manufacturer or an importer with a testing capacity at a level equivalent to or higher than the level specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;
Where the safety of a product subject to safety certification has been confirmed and is imported through parallel importation, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;
Other cases specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those where safety is approved under any other statute.
Article 17 (Safety Inspections on Imported Used Electrical Appliances subject to Safety Verification)

A person who intends to import used electrical appliances subject to safety verification from a foreign country shall undergo a safety inspection conducted in order to verify the safety of the relevant electrical appliances subject to safety verification, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the foregoing shall not apply where there is a ground to exempt a person from the duty to file a safety verification report under any subparagraph of Article 16 .
The safety standards under Article 15 (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the standards for safety inspections under paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
Article 18 (Marking of Products subject to Safety Verification)

A manufacturer or an importer of products subject to safety verification shall put any of the marks specified in the following subparagraphs (hereinafter referred to as "safety verification mark or a similar mark") on the products subject to safety verification or packages of such products, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
Products subject to safety certification for which a safety verification report has been filed: The safety verification mark and the mark specified in the safety standards under Article 15 (4);

Products subject to safety verification, for which a person is exempted from the duty to file a safety verification report under Article 16 : The mark of exemption from the duty to report safety verification;

Electrical appliances subject to safety verification, which have passed a safety inspection conducted under Article 17 (1): The safety inspection mark and the mark specified in the standards for safety inspection under Article 17 (2).

No person shall put the safety verification mark or a similar mark on a product subject to safety verification and packages of such product, unless the person has filed a safety verification report, is exempted from the duty to file a safety verification report under Article 16 , or has successfully passed a safety inspection under Article 17 (1).
Any of the following persons shall not modify or remove the safety verification mark or a similar mark of products subject to safety verification, without permission:
A manufacturer, an importer or an import agent of products subject to safety verification;
A distributor, a sales broker or a buying agent of products subject to safety verification;
A rental business operator of products subject to safety verification;
A person who produces a product by using a product subject to safety verification as a component or part;
The following persons who use electrical appliances subject to safety verification:
An electric utility business operator defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A person who builds electric installations for private use as defined in subparagraph 19 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A constructor defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Electrical Construction Business Act ;
A person who uses consumer products subject to safety verification for commercial purposes.

Where a person referred to in any subparagraph of paragraph (3) engages in the distribution, rental, sales brokerage (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce , Etc. removes a product without the safety verification mark or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety verification mark or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information) or import agency through the Internet, such person shall post information related to safety verification in the relevant website so that consumers can find such information, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 19 (Prohibition of Distribution and Use of Products subject to Safety Verification Without Safety Verification Mark or Similar Mark)

A manufacturer, importer, distributor or rental business operator of products subject to safety verification shall neither sell or rent any product subject to safety verification without the safety verification mark or a similar mark, nor import, display, or store such product for the purpose of selling or renting such product.

No sales broker, buying agent or import agent of products subject to safety verification shall handle such products without the safety verification mark similar mark as a sales broker (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce removes a product without the safety verification mark or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety verification mark or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information), buying agent, or import agent.
Any person referred to in any subparagraph of Article 18 (3) 4 through 6 shall not use a product subject to safety verification without the safety verification mark or a similar mark.
Article 20 (Invalidation of Safety Verification Reports)

In any of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may invalidate the safety verification report filed by a manufacturer or importer of products subject to safety verification or may issue an order to forbid the use of the safety verification mark or a similar mark or to make improvements within a specified period of not more than six months, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That a safety verification report shall be invalidated in cases falling under subparagraph 1: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If it is found that a manufacturer or importer of products subject to safety verification files a safety verification report by fraud or other improper means;
If the product subject to safety verification fails to conform to the safety standards under Article 15 (4);
If a manufacturer or importer of products subject to safety verification has not put the safety verification mark or a similar mark or fraudulently put any mark;
If a manufacturer or importer of products subject to safety verification violates an order issued under Article 40 (2) or (9).

When the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy invalidates a safety verification report or issues an order to prohibit the use of the safety verification mark or a similar mark or to make improvements under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly announce such fact, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

If a safety verification report is invalidated under paragraph (1), no testing lab for safety verification shall test any model identical to the relevant project for safety verification during one year after the date on which the report is invalidated.
Article 21 (Revocation of Designation of Testing Labs for Safety Verification)

If a testing lab for safety verification falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may fully or partially revoke the designation of the testing lab for safety verification or order it to fully or partially suspend its business operations for a specified period of up to one year: Provided , That the designation shall be revoked in cases falling under subparagraph 1 or 2: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If it has been designated as a testing lab for safety verification by fraud or other improper means;

If a testing lab for safety verification continues tests for safety verification or safety inspections during the period of suspension of business operations after it is ordered to suspend business operations;
If a testing lab for safety verification fails to conduct tests for safety verification or safety inspections, without good cause;

If a testing lab for safety verification violates any of methods, procedures, etc. of tests for safety verification or safety inspections in performing tests for safety verification or safety inspections;
If a testing lab for safety verification ceases to meet the standards for designation under Article 14 (2);
If a testing lab for safety verification fails to prepare and retain records of tests for safety verification or prepares and retains false records, in violation of Article 14 (4);
If a testing lab for safety verification violates safety standards under Article 15 (4) in performing tests for safety verification;
If a testing lab for safety verification violates Article 20 (3) in conducting tests for safety verification;
If a testing lab for safety verification charges a fee at a rate higher or lower than the rate specified under Article 43 .

The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall not designate a person as a testing lab for safety verification again within one year from the date the person has its designation revoked under paragraph (1).
Detailed criteria for the administrative dispositions under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 22 (Penalty Surcharges Imposed in Lieu of Suspension of Business Operations for Testing for Safety Verification)

If the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy has to order a person to suspend business operations under any subparagraph of Article 21 (1) but finds that the suspension of business operations will cause severe inconvenience to users of the business, he or she may impose a penalty surcharge of up to 300 million won upon the person, in lieu of the suspension of business operations.

Matters necessary for the amount of a penalty surcharge to be imposed under paragraph (1) for each type of violation according to the degree of violation, etc., the method of collecting such penalty surcharge, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

If a person who is obligated to pay a penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) fails to pay the penalty surcharge by payment deadline, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall collect the penalty surcharge in the same manner as delinquent national taxes are collected.
Article 23 (Supplier's Declaration of Conformity)

A manufacturer or an importer of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity shall directly conduct product tests for each model of the products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity or shall request a third party to conduct product tests on its behalf and shall verify for itself that the relevant products conform to the safety standards under paragraph (4), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

When a manufacturer or an importer of electrical appliances subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity declares the conformity of a specific product, as the supplier of the product, under paragraph (1), such manufacturer or importer shall report the details of verification (hereinafter referred to as "report on the supplier's declaration of conformity") to the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy. The same procedure shall also apply where it is intended to make a change in any of the reported matters.

Upon receipt of a report or a report on change under paragraph (2), the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall review the details thereof and accept such report if it conforms to this Act. <Added on Oct. 18, 2022>

The supplier's declaration of conformity under paragraph (1) shall be made in accordance with the safety standards determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy for products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity: Provided , That the supplier's declaration of conformity may be made, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, if there are no safety standards publicly notified for a specific product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity or if it is impracticable to apply the safety standards publicly notified to a specific product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

A manufacturer or an importer who declares the conformity of a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity under paragraph (1) shall keep documents demonstrating that the product conforms to the safety standards under paragraph (4), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
Article 24 (Exemption from Supplier's Duty to Declare Conformity)

Where a person obtains confirmation from the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy on the products specified by Presidential Decree, from among those subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity, and produced or imported for the purpose of research and development, exhibition, or testing of products for the supplier's declaration of conformity, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;

Where a person obtains confirmation from a Mayor/ Do Governor on the products specified by Presidential Decree, from among those subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity, and produced or imported for the purpose of exportation, as prescribed by municipal ordinance of the relevant City/ Do ;
Where products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity are produced for the purpose of exportation;

Where the safety of a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity has been confirmed and is imported through parallel importation, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy;
Other cases specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those the safety of which is approved by any other statute.
Article 25 (Marking of Products subject to Supplier's Declaration of Conformity)

A manufacturer or an importer of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity shall put the mark specified in either of the following subparagraphs (hereinafter referred to as "mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark") on the products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity or packages of such products, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>

Where a product is subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity and the supplier declares the conformity of the product or has filed a report on the supplier's declaration of conformity: The mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity and the mark specified in the safety standards under Article 23 (4);

Where a product is subject to the supplier's declaration or reporting of conformity but the supplier is exempted from the duty to declare the conformity of such product or to report the conformity of such product under Article 24 : The mark of exemption.

A person who fails to declare the conformity of the product or file a report on the declaration of such product as a supplier or a person who is not exempt from the duty to declare or to report the supplier’s conformity of said product shall not put the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark on the products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity and packages of such products.
Any of the following persons shall not modify or remove the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity on a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity, without permission:
A manufacturer, an importer, or an import agent of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity;
A distributor or a sales broker of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity;
A rental business operator of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity;
A person who produces a product by using a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity as a component or part;
The following persons who use electrical appliances subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity:
An electric utility business operator defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A person who builds electric installations for private use as defined in subparagraph 19 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A constructor defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Electrical Construction Business Act ;
A person who uses consumer products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity for commercial purposes.

Where a person referred to in any subparagraph of paragraph (3) engages in the distribution, rental, sales brokerage (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce , Etc. removes a product without the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information) or import agency through the Internet, the person shall publish information about the supplier's declaration of conformity in the relevant website so that consumers can find such information, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 26 (Prohibition against Distribution, Use, etc. of Products subject to Supplier's Declaration of Conformity Without Mark of Supplier's Declaration of Conformity or Similar Mark)

Any manufacturer, importer, distributor or rental business operator of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity shall neither sell or rent any product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity without the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark, nor import, display, or store such product for the purpose of selling or renting such product.

Any sales broker or import agent of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity shall not act as a sales broker (excluding cases where a mail order broker defined by the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce removes a product without the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark immediately when he or she finds such product from the cyber mall operated by the person and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark when they register commodities, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information) or import agent of products subject to safety verification without the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark.

No person referred to in any subparagraph of Article 25 (3) 4 through 6 shall use a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity without the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark.
Article 27 (Prohibition against Use of Mark of Supplier's Declaration of Conformity or Similar Mark)

In any of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may issue an order to forbid a manufacturer or an importer of the products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity from using the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark for a specified period of up to six months or to take measures for improvement, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That an order shall be issued to forbid such manufacturer or importer from using the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark in cases falling under subparagraph 1: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If it is found that a manufacturer or an importer has made or reported the supplier’s declaration of conformity by fraud or other improper means;
If a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity fails to conform to the safety standards under Article 23 (4);
If a manufacturer or an importer fails to put the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark or fraudulently puts such mark;
If a manufacturer or an importer violates an order issued under Article 40 (3) or (9).

When the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy issues an order to forbid a person from using the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark or to take measures for improvement under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly announce such fact, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 28 (Consumer Products subject to Compliance with Safety Standards)
Article 29 (Marking of Products subject to Compliance with Safety Standards)

A manufacturer or an importer of consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards shall put the mark specified in the safety standards under Article 28 on the products subject to compliance with safety standards or packages of such products, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

A person referred to in either of the following subparagraphs shall not modify or remove the mark of a consumer product subject to compliance with safety standards under paragraph (1), without permission:
A manufacturer, an importer or an import agent of consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards;
A distributor or a sales broker of consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards.
Article 30 (Prohibition of Distribution, Use, etc. of Consumer Products subject to Compliance with Safety Standards with No Proper Marking)
Article 31 (Order to Improve Marking of Consumer Products subject to Compliance with Safety Standards)

In either of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may order a manufacturer or an importer of consumer products subject to compliance with safety standards to make improvements within a specified period of not more than six months, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy:
If any consumer product subject to compliance with safety standards does not meet the safety standards under Article 28 ;
If a manufacturer or an importer fails to put the mark specified in Article 29 (1) or fraudulently puts such mark.

When the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy issues an order for improvement under paragraph (1), he or she shall publicly announce such fact, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 32 (Reporting of Consumer Products subject to Child Protective Packaging)

A manufacturer or an importer who produces or imports consumer products subject to child protective packaging shall use child protective packaging materials for such products: Provided, the foregoing shall not apply to the products approved by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, from among the following products:
Products produced or imported for the purpose of selling them to manufacturers;
Products produced or imported for the purpose of research and development or exportation.

When a manufacturer or an importer of consumer products subject to child protective packaging uses child protective packaging materials in accordance with the main clause of paragraph (1), it shall report the details thereof for each model of consumer products subject to child protective packaging to the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy. The same procedure shall also apply where it is intended to make a change in any of the reported matters.

Upon receipt of a report or a report on change under paragraph (2), the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall review the details thereof and accept such report if it conforms to this Act. <Added on Oct. 18, 2022>
The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall determine and publicly notify safety standards applicable to consumer products subject to child protective packaging. <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
Article 33 (Marking of Child Protective Packaging)

If a manufacturer or an importer of consumer products subject to child protective packaging has filed a report in accordance with Article 32 (2), it shall put a mark indicating that child protective packaging materials are used on the relevant consumer products subject to child protective packaging and packaging materials of such products (hereinafter referred to as "mark of child protective packaging"), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

No person shall put the mark of child protective packaging or any similar mark or label on any consumer product subject to child protective packaging and packages of such product without filing a report in accordance with Article 32 (2).
Article 34 (Restriction on Sales)
Article 34-2 (Designation of Safety Inspection Institutions)

The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may designate a manufacturer of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection, or a corporation or organization that conducts the affairs related to safety control of products as an institution that conducts safety inspections, in order to ensure the safety of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection.

A person who intends to be designated as an institution that conducts safety inspections under paragraph (1) shall meet the standards for designation prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as inspection facilities and human resources required for safety inspections, and shall file an application for designation with the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
A safety inspection institution shall prepare and retain records related to safety inspections, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may guide, supervise, and assist safety inspection institutions to the extent necessary for ensuring the safety of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection.
Article 34-3 (Safety Inspections)
A manufacturer of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection shall have such appliances undergo safety inspections, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

A safety inspection institution shall conduct safety inspections in accordance with the safety standards for electrical appliances subject to safety inspection determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the safety inspection institution may conduct safety inspections, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, if safety standards have not been publicly notified or the safety standards publicly notified are not applicable.

Where a manufacturer of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection has such appliances undergo safety inspections under paragraph (1), he or she shall keep documents demonstrating that the relevant electrical appliances subject to safety inspection meet the safety standards under the main clause of paragraph (2) (referring to the standards prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, in the case of a safety inspection under the proviso of that paragraph), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 34-4 (Safety Inspection Mark of Electrical Appliances Subject to Safety Inspection)

A safety inspection institution and a manufacturer of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection shall put a safety inspection mark on electrical appliances subject to safety inspection that undergo safety inspections and a mark (hereinafter referred to as "safety inspection mark, etc.") specified in the safety standards under the main clause of Article 34-3 (2) (referring the standards prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, where a safety inspection is conducted under the proviso of that paragraph), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.

A person who does not conduct a safety inspection or fails to have electrical appliances subject to safety inspection undergo safety inspections shall not put a safety inspection mark, etc. or a similar mark on electrical appliances subject to safety inspection.
Any of the following persons shall not modify or remove a safety inspection mark, etc. put on electrical appliances subject to safety inspection, without permission:
A manufacturer, a distributor, a sales broker, or a rental business operator of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection;
A person who produces products by using electrical appliances subject to safety inspection as components or parts;
Any of the following persons who use electrical appliances subject to safety inspection:
An electric utility business entity defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A person who establishes electric installations for private use defined in subparagraph 19 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act ;
A constructor defined in subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Electrical Construction Business Act ;
A person who uses electrical appliances subject to safety inspection for commercial purposes.

Where a person falling under any subparagraph of paragraph (3) engages in the distribution, rental, or sales brokerage of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection through the Internet, such person shall post information related to safety inspection on the relevant website so that consumers can find such information, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy: Provided , That the foregoing shall not apply where a mail order broker under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce immediately removes electrical appliances subject to safety inspection without a safety inspection mark, etc. when he or she finds such appliances from the cyber mall operated by him or her and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety inspection mark, etc. when they register products, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information.
Article 34-5 (Prohibition of Distribution and Use of Electrical Appliances Subject to Safety Inspection Without Safety Inspection Mark)

A manufacturer, importer, distributor, or rental business operator of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection shall not sell or rent such appliances without a safety inspection mark, etc. or shall not display or store the appliances for the purpose of selling or renting them.

No sales broker of electrical appliances subject to safety inspection shall engage in sales brokerage for such appliances without a safety inspection mark, etc.; provided, the foregoing shall not apply where a mail order broker under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce immediately removes electrical appliances subject to safety inspection without a safety inspection mark, etc. when he or she finds such appliances from the cyber mall operated by him or her and requires persons requesting mail order brokerage to enter information about the safety inspection mark, etc. when they register products, while taking technical measures to ensure that consumers can find such information.
No person falling under any subparagraph of Article 34 (4) 2 through 4 shall use electrical appliances subject to safety inspection without a safety inspection mark, etc.
Article 34-6 (Revocation of Designation of Safety Inspection Institutions)

If a safety inspection institution falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy may fully or partially revoke the designation of the institution or order it to fully or partially suspend its business operations for a specified period not exceeding one year: Provided , That the designation shall be revoked in cases falling under subparagraph 1 or 2:
If it has been designated as a safety inspection institution by fraud or other improper means;
If it conducts safety inspections during the period of suspension of business operations after it is ordered to suspend business operations;
If it fails to conduct safety inspections without good reason;
If it fails to comply with methods, procedures, etc. for safety inspections when conducting safety inspections;
If it ceases to meet the standards for designation under Article 34-2 (2);
If it fails to prepare and retain records related to safety inspections or prepares and retains false records, in violation of Article 34-2 (3);

If it fails to comply with the safety standards under the main clause of Article 34-3 (2) (referring to the standards prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, where a safety inspection is conducted under the proviso of that paragraph) when conducting safety inspections;
If it charges a fee at a rate higher or lower than the rate prescribed in Article 43 .

The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall not designate a person as a safety inspection institution again within one year from the date the person has its designation revoked under paragraph (1).
Detailed criteria for the administrative dispositions under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 34-7 (Penalty Surcharges Imposed in Lieu of Suspension of Business Operations of Safety Inspection Institutions)

If the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy has to order a person to suspend business operations under Article 34-6 (1) but finds that the suspension of business operations are likely to cause severe inconvenience to users of the business, he or she may impose a penalty surcharge of up to 300 million won upon the person, in lieu of the suspension of business operations.

If a person who is obligated to pay a penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) fails to pay the penalty surcharge by the payment deadline, the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy shall collect the penalty surcharge in the same manner as national taxes are compulsorily collected.

Matters necessary for the amount of a penalty surcharge to be imposed under paragraph (1) for the type and severity of a violation, the method of collecting such penalty surcharge, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
Article 34-8 (Request for Sharing Information for Safety Inspections)
Article 34-9 (Liability for Compensation)
Where a safety inspection institution poorly conducts a safety inspection by intent or negligence and causes any loss to other persons, it shall compensate them for such loss.

In order to ensure liability for compensation for loss under paragraph (1), a safety inspection institution shall purchase insurance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, or shall join a capital goods mutual aid association under Article 40 (1) 1 of the Industrial Development Act or take other necessary measures.
Article 35 (Special Provisions concerning Buying Services)

Products specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, among products subject to safety certification but without the safety certification mark or a similar mark, considering the usage, the degree of hazard, etc. of such products;

Products specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy, among electrical appliances subject to safety verification but without the safety verification mark or a similar mark, considering the usage, the degree of hazard, etc. of such products;
Consumer products subject to safety verification but without the safety verification mark or a similar mark.
Article 36 (Duty of Notification by Buying Agents)

A buying agent shall give notice of the following information (referring to notice posted on the relevant website in cases of buying services provided through the Internet) to buyers (hereinafter referred to as "notice concerning buying services"), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy:
The fact that the relevant products are distributed through buying services;
The fact that the relevant products are subject to safety control under this Act;
Information about the marking of safety certification or reporting of safety verification of the relevant product;
Other facts specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those deemed necessary for consumer safety.

When a buying agent becomes aware that a defect in any product provided through buying services or any product identical to such product caused or is likely to cause harm or damage to the life, body or property of a consumer, the buying agent shall discontinue buying services for such product.
Matters necessary for the criteria, procedure, etc. for the discontinuance of buying services under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 37 (Order to Discontinue Buying Services for Products Eligible for Buying Services)

When the Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy finds that a defect in any product provided through buying services or any product identical to such product caused or is likely to cause harm or damage to the life, health or property of a consumer, he or she may order the relevant buying agent to discontinue buying services for such product.
Matters necessary for the order to discontinue buying services under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy.
Article 38 (Duty of Parallel Importers to Put Labels)

Where a person imports products subject to safety certification, safety verification or the supplier's declaration of conformity or exempted from safety certification, the reporting of safety verification, the supplier's declaration of conformity or the reporting of the supplier's declaration of conformity under subparagraph 7 of Article 6 , subparagraph 6 of Article 16 or subparagraph 4 of Article 24 , through parallel importation, such person shall put a label of the following facts (hereinafter referred to as "label of parallel importation") on such products or packages of such products and shall give notice of the following information (referring to notice posted on the relevant website if such products are sold through the Internet) to buyers, if such person sells the products (including cases where such person sells the products through the Internet):
The fact that the relevant products were imported through parallel importation;
The fact that the relevant products are subject to safety control under this Act;
Other facts specified by Ministerial Decree of Trade, Industry and Energy as those deemed necessary for consumer safety.

No person shall put a label of parallel importation on any product not imported through parallel importation, from among products subject to safety certification, safety verification or the supplier's declaration of conformity.
Article 39 (Restriction on Sales by Age Eligible for Use)
Article 40 (Order to Improve, Destroy, or Recall Products subject to Safety Control or to Suspend Sales of such Products, etc.)

In any of the following cases, a Mayor/ Do Governor may issue an order to any manufacturer, importer, distributor, rental business operator, or commercial user (referring to a person who falls under Article 9 (3) 6, 18 (3) 6, 25 (3) 6, or 34-4 (3) 4; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply), sales broker, buying agent, or import agent of products subject to safety certification to improve, destroy, or recall any product subject to safety certification or suspend sales of such product (hereinafter referred to as "suspend sales or take other required measure") within a specified period, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If a product subject to safety certification has no safety certification under Article 5 (1);
If a product subject to safety certification has no revised certification under the main clause of Article 5 (2);

If a product subject to safety certification fails to meet the safety standards under Article 5 (3) (referring to the standards that have been applied to the safety certification issued under the proviso of the that paragraph; including cases to which the standards shall be applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 8 (2)) or the standards for factory assessment;
If a product subject to safety certification has not undergone the safety inspection under Article 8 (1);

If a person has not put the safety certification mark or a similar mark on a products subject to safety certification, in violation of Article 9 (1), despite the fact that the safety of the product was certified;
If a person puts the safety certification mark or a similar mark, in violation of Article 9 (2);
If a person modifies or removes the safety certification mark or a similar mark, without permission, in violation of Article 9 (3);

If a person sells or rents a product subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark or imports, displays, or stores such product, in violation of Article 10 (1), for the purpose of selling or renting the product;

If a person acts as a sales broker, buying agent or import agent for a product subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark, in violation of Article 10 (2) (excluding cases where a person acts as a buying agent pursuant to Article 35 (1));
If a person uses a product subject to safety certification without the safety certification mark or a similar mark, in violation of Article 10 (3).

In any of the following cases, a Mayor/ Do Governor may order any manufacturer, importer, distributor, rental business operator, commercial user, sales broker, buying agent, or import agent of products subject to safety verification to suspend sales of any product subject to safety verification or to take other required measures for a specified period, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If a person fails to file a report in accordance with Article 15 (1);
If a person fails to file a report on change in accordance with the main clause of Article 15 (2);

If a product subject to safety verification fails to meet the safety standards under Article 15 (4) (referring to the standards that have been applied to tests conducted for safety verification under the proviso of the that paragraph; including cases applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 17 (2));
If a product subject to safety verification has not undergone the safety inspection under Article 17 (1);
If a person has not put the safety verification mark or a similar mark, in violation of Article 18 (1);
If a person puts the safety verification mark or any similar mark or label, in violation of Article 18 (2);
If a person modifies or removes the safety verification mark or a similar mark, without permission, in violation of Article 18 (3);

If a person sells or rents a product subject to safety verification without the safety verification mark or a similar mark or imports, displays or stores such products for the purpose of selling or renting the product, in violation of Article 19 (1);

If a person acts as a sales broker, buying agent or import agent for a product subject to safety verification without the safety verification mark or a similar mark (excluding cases where a person acts as a buying agent pursuant to subparagraph 2 or 3 of Article 35) , in violation of Article 19 (2);
If a person uses a product subject to safety verification without the safety verification mark or a similar mark, in violation of Article 19 (3).

In any of the following cases, a Mayor/ Do Governor may order any manufacturer, importer, distributor, rental business operator, commercial user, sales broker, or import agent of products subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity to suspend sales of any product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity or to take other required measures for a specified period, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
If a person fails to make a supplier’s declaration of conformity;

If a product subject to the supplier's declaration of conformity fail to meet the safety standards under Article 23 (4) (referring to the standards applicable to the supplier's declaration of conformity under the proviso of the that paragraph, if a product falls under the proviso of the that paragraph);
If a person fails to put the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark, in violation of Article 25 (1);
If a person puts the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or any similar mark or label, in violation of Article 25 (2);
If a person modifies or removes the mark of the supplier's declaration of conformity or a similar mark, without permission, in violation of Article 25 (3);
